### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`  _(via duration_ms (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a32d50b666b05aa108417ba16c2b71285cbee87e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b4050eaab27b3597f9cd7db029b5382267aa3ce9` — the merge of head `78734648ae2c64a9a62e806e0c54c29aff099b60` into base `a32d50b666b05aa108417ba16c2b71285cbee87e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b4050eaab27b3597f9cd7db029b5382267aa3ce9 && git checkout b4050eaab27b3597f9cd7db029b5382267aa3ce9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a32d50b666b05aa108417ba16c2b71285cbee87e 78734648ae2c64a9a62e806e0c54c29aff099b60 && git checkout -B drift-repro a32d50b666b05aa108417ba16c2b71285cbee87e && git merge --no-ff 78734648ae2c64a9a62e806e0c54c29aff099b60

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a32d50b666b05aa108417ba16c2b71285cbee87e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a32d50b666b05aa108417ba16c2b71285cbee87e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `78734648ae2c64a9a62e806e0c54c29aff099b60`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the changeset and the refreshed PR body is true and complete against the diff. The new exports `TurnCost`, `TurnTime`, `ModelSpend`, `AskSpend`, `turnCost`, `turnTime`, `askSpend`, `authorTimeText`, `askCostText`, `askTimeText`, `guardrailTally` and `GuardrailVerdict` live in `scorecard.ts`. The new optional fields are `ModeScorecard` / `CardScorecard` `.authorTime` / `.askSpend`, `HalfScores.guardrails`, `TurnSummary.reportedDurationMs` / `reportedApiDurationMs` and `ParsedTurn.meta.reportedDurationMs` / `reportedApiDurationMs`. All reach `./runner` through `export *`. `AuthorCost` becomes a type alias of `TurnCost` with the same three fields. `authorCost()` keeps its signature and result, and `authorCostText` its output, so no reader changes. The answer that moves is declared. The scorecard adds `Author time`, `Ask cost` and `Ask time` rows per mode and lines per card. Ask figures are grouped by served model over every question and operation turn of the Run half and the iterate. Cost follows the author-cost rule (stated only when every counted turn reported one). Time is the runner's own `elapsedMs`, stated only when every counted turn was timed, otherwise "N of M not timed", never a smaller sum or a zero. A record written before the rows reads `not recorded`. The CLI's `duration_ms` / `duration_api_ms` are recorded on the turn and not summed. The `Run · guardrails` / `Iterate · Run · guardrails` rows state `RunHalf.guardrails` (#33738) as pass, fail or `not measured: <reason>`, and are absent when no half carries any.

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset bumps it. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: nothing a metadata author writes (spec, app metadata, card JSON) is added, narrowed or changed in meaning. The widening is additive exports and optional fields of the evaluation package `@objectstack/scenarios`. No existing export is removed, renamed or narrowed in type.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, no runtime or security behaviour of the platform. No grader verdict moves: the scorecard only sums and states what the record already carries. The grader stays deterministic (cloud#3600 cost ruling).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-dg3roj`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qiby1cctpVpRbJzjccvY`

**VERDICT: PASS**
